system.overview: The Light RailLink is a light rail system operated by the Maryland Transit Administration serving the Baltimore metropolitan area. Running 30 miles from Hunt Valley in northern Baltimore County through downtown Baltimore to Cromwell Station/Glen Burnie and BWI Airport in Anne Arundel County, it is one of the oldest modern light rail systems in the eastern United States. The system uses former railroad rights-of-way for much of its route and runs as a street-running railway through downtown on Howard Street.

history.title: Limited Service Opens
history.description: Light RailLink opens with limited service from Timonium Fairgrounds to Camden Yards for Baltimore Orioles games at the new Oriole Park at Camden Yards.

history.title: Full Daily Service Begins
history.description: Full daily service begins on the initial 9.4-mile segment from Timonium Fairgrounds to Camden Yards, comprising 14 stations.

history.title: Southern Extension Completed
history.description: Final southern stations open to Cromwell Station/Glen Burnie, completing the original 22.5-mile main line from Timonium to Glen Burnie.

history.title: Hunt Valley Extension
history.description: Line extended 4.5 miles north from Timonium to Hunt Valley, adding five new stations including park-and-ride facilities.

history.title: BWI Airport Branch and Penn Station Spur Open
history.description: Two short branches added: a 2.7-mile spur to BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport terminal and a 0.3-mile spur connecting to Penn Station for Amtrak and MARC transfers.

history.title: Hamburg Street Station Opens
history.description: Infill station opens adjacent to the new Ravens stadium (now M&T Bank Stadium), initially serving game days only. Later renamed Stadium/Federal Hill.

history.title: Double-Tracking Project Begins
history.description: Major $205 million reconstruction project to double-track most of the system begins. Southern section closed through much of 2004; northern section closed January–October 2005.

history.title: Double-Tracking Completed
history.description: Full service restored after completion of the double-tracking project, significantly improving frequency and reliability across the system.

history.title: Fleet Replacement Grant Awarded
history.description: MTA awarded $213.7 million federal grant to replace the entire 53-vehicle Light Rail fleet with new modern railcars as part of the Light Rail Modernization Program.

main-line.name: Hunt Valley – Cromwell/Glen Burnie
main-line.description: The main north-south line running from Hunt Valley in northern Baltimore County through downtown Baltimore on Howard Street to Cromwell Station/Glen Burnie in Anne Arundel County. The line follows the former Northern Central Railway right-of-way north of downtown and the former Baltimore and Annapolis Railroad alignment to the south.

bwi-branch.name: BWI Airport Branch
bwi-branch.description: A 2.7-mile branch diverging from the main line near Linthicum, serving the BWI Business District and BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport terminal. Partially single-tracked.

penn-camden-shuttle.name: Penn-Camden Shuttle
penn-camden-shuttle.description: A shuttle service running between Penn Station and Camden Yards via the downtown Howard Street corridor. Penn Station is connected via a 0.3-mile single-track spur from the main line near University of Baltimore/Mt Royal. Operates every 30 minutes with single-car trains.

hunt-valley.name: Hunt Valley
hunt-valley.description: Northern terminus of the Light RailLink system, located in Hunt Valley, Baltimore County. Large park-and-ride facility.

pepper-road.name: Pepper Road
pepper-road.description: Surface station in the Hunt Valley area, opened as part of the 1997 northern extension.

mccormick-road.name: McCormick Road
mccormick-road.description: Surface station near McCormick & Company headquarters in Hunt Valley.

gilroy-road.name: Gilroy Road
gilroy-road.description: Surface station in the Timonium area of Baltimore County.

warren-road.name: Warren Road
warren-road.description: Surface station with park-and-ride facility in the Timonium area.

fairgrounds.name: Fairgrounds
fairgrounds.description: Formerly Timonium Fairgrounds, this was the original northern terminus when the system opened in 1992. Located adjacent to the Maryland State Fairgrounds.

timonium-business-park.name: Timonium Business Park
timonium-business-park.description: Surface station serving the Timonium business park area of Baltimore County.

lutherville.name: Lutherville
lutherville.description: Surface station with park-and-ride facility in the Lutherville-Timonium community.

falls-road.name: Falls Road
falls-road.description: Surface station with park-and-ride facility adjacent to Lake Roland and the Robert E. Lee Memorial Park.

mt-washington.name: Mt Washington
mt-washington.description: Surface station in the Mt Washington neighborhood of Baltimore.

cold-spring-lane.name: Cold Spring Lane
cold-spring-lane.description: Surface station at Cold Spring Lane in northern Baltimore.

woodberry.name: Woodberry
woodberry.description: Surface station in the Woodberry neighborhood, near the Meadow Mill development and Clipper Mill.

north-avenue.name: North Avenue
north-avenue.description: Street-running station on Howard Street at North Avenue. Adjacent to the light rail maintenance facility. Served by both the main line and Penn-Camden shuttle.

university-of-baltimore-mt-royal.name: University of Baltimore/Mt Royal
university-of-baltimore-mt-royal.description: Street-running station on Howard Street near the University of Baltimore and Maryland Institute College of Art. The Penn Station spur diverges near this station.

cultural-center.name: Cultural Center
cultural-center.description: Street-running station on Howard Street near the Lyric Opera House and Joseph Meyerhoff Symphony Hall. Walking distance to the Metro SubwayLink State Center station.

centre-street.name: Centre Street
centre-street.description: Street-running station on Howard Street at Centre Street in downtown Baltimore.

lexington-market.name: Lexington Market
lexington-market.description: Street-running station on Howard Street adjacent to the historic Lexington Market. Transfer point to the Metro SubwayLink system via a short walk to the underground metro station.

university-center-baltimore-street.name: University Center/Baltimore Street
university-center-baltimore-street.description: Street-running station on Howard Street at Baltimore Street, near the University of Maryland, Baltimore campus.

convention-center.name: Convention Center
convention-center.description: Street-running station on Howard Street near the Baltimore Convention Center.

camden-yards.name: Camden Yards
camden-yards.description: Street-running station near Oriole Park at Camden Yards and the historic Camden Station. Southern terminus of the Penn-Camden shuttle. Adjacent to the Camden MARC station for Amtrak and MARC Camden Line service.

stadium-federal-hill.name: Stadium/Federal Hill
stadium-federal-hill.description: Infill station formerly known as Hamburg Street, opened in 1998 adjacent to M&T Bank Stadium (home of the Baltimore Ravens). Initially a game-day-only stop, it became a full-time daily station in 2005.

westport.name: Westport
westport.description: Surface station in the Westport neighborhood of South Baltimore.

cherry-hill.name: Cherry Hill
cherry-hill.description: Surface station serving the Cherry Hill community of South Baltimore.

patapsco.name: Patapsco
patapsco.description: Surface station near the Patapsco River crossing. The BWI Airport branch diverges south of this station.

baltimore-highlands.name: Baltimore Highlands
baltimore-highlands.description: Surface station in the Baltimore Highlands community of Anne Arundel County.

nursery-road.name: Nursery Road
nursery-road.description: Surface station with park-and-ride facility near Nursery Road in Linthicum Heights.

north-linthicum.name: North Linthicum
north-linthicum.description: Surface station in the North Linthicum area of Anne Arundel County.

linthicum.name: Linthicum
linthicum.description: Junction station where the BWI Airport branch diverges from the main line. Park-and-ride facility available.

ferndale.name: Ferndale
ferndale.description: Surface station in the Ferndale community of Anne Arundel County.

cromwell-station-glen-burnie.name: Cromwell Station/Glen Burnie
cromwell-station-glen-burnie.description: Southern terminus of the main line, located in Glen Burnie, Anne Arundel County. Large park-and-ride facility.

bwi-business-district.name: BWI Business District
bwi-business-district.description: Surface station serving the BWI Business District office park area near the airport.

bwi-airport.name: BWI Airport
bwi-airport.description: Terminus of the BWI Airport branch, providing direct rail access to BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport. Connected to the airport terminal via a covered walkway.

penn-station.name: Penn Station
penn-station.description: Northern terminus of the Penn-Camden shuttle, located adjacent to Baltimore Penn Station. Provides connections to Amtrak Northeast Corridor and MARC Penn Line commuter rail services.

railcars.name: ABB LRV (5001–5035)
railcars.description: The original 35 articulated light rail vehicles, numbered 5001–5035, were the first transit vehicles in the United States to employ AC propulsion. Each three-section car is powered via pantograph from 750V DC overhead catenary. They were the widest LRVs in the US at delivery at 9 ft 6 in.

railcars.name: ADtranz LRV (5036–5053)
railcars.description: 18 additional vehicles, numbered 5036–5053, were delivered in 1997–1999 to support the Hunt Valley extension and BWI Airport branch. Built by AAI Corporation under the ADtranz brand (successor to ABB Traction), they are functionally identical to the original fleet. The entire 53-car fleet is slated for replacement under the Light Rail Modernization Program.
